root_idea.summary: The root centers on the female or feminine as opposed to the male, with associated extensions involving softness, yieldingness, and the receptive or passive side.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from sex and grammatical gender to soft iron, fertile and even land, and figurative applications to things treated as feminine or passive. Quran-focused interpretation also applies the term polemically to inanimate idols as non-agent beings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular feminine noun citation form.
This group is the inflected dual of أُنْثَى and does not constitute a separate lexical headword.

senses.definition: A female; feminine as opposed to male, applied to a female being or to anything classed as feminine.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran this includes human and animal females, the feminine gender, and the dual expression “two females.” The noun may also occur in plural usage as إِنَاثٌ.

senses.definition: A Quranic polemical designation of idols or other inanimate objects as “females.”
senses.usage_conditions: In the relevant Quranic passages, this is interpreted either from the grammatically feminine names of the deities or from their being inanimate, passive, and incapable of hearing, seeing, or acting; it is not a claim that the objects possess biological sex.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become female, feminine, or of the feminine gender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb; the feminine classification may apply to a person, animal, noun, or other thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land or ground: plain, even, soft, and fertile, especially producing abundant herbage; of a place, one where vegetation grows quickly and abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for land or a place characterized by softness, evenness, and good growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or yielding iron; by extension, a sword made of such iron, or a blunt and non-sharp sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description contrasts with hard or sharp “male” iron and may describe either the metal or a sword made from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a noun or another syntactically dependent word feminine by attaching the sign of the feminine gender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II grammatical construction concerning the marking or treatment of a word as feminine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a person effeminate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended use of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act gently toward someone, or to proceed gently in a matter; an alternative characterization describes the manner as effeminate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with لَهُ toward a person and with فِي أَمْرِهِ in relation to an affair or undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman: to bring forth a female or females.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV verb describing childbirth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A feminine woman; conventionally, a perfect or exemplary woman, as a term of praise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of a woman, not merely a neutral statement of biological sex.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small stars.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two testicles; in some usage, the scrotum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized dual anatomical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized dual expression associated with the feminine grammatical gender of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two tribes of Bejeeleh and Kudāʿah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific conventional tribal designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The inner parts of a horse’s thighs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical expression referring to the two inner thigh parts of a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manjaniq, the engine of war known as a catapult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized designation attributed to the feminine gender of the word manjaniq.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The female or feminine nature, quality, or gender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun for femininity or feminine classification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who bears a female or females.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun describing the woman in relation to the sex of her offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who usually bears female children, or a man who usually begets female children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation applies to either sex; its counterpart is the term for one who usually produces male children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Feminine or made feminine, especially a feminine word or grammatical form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a word that is intrinsically feminine or has been assigned feminine treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An effeminate man, one resembling a woman in gentleness, softness of speech, languor of movement, or bodily form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal description distinct from grammatical femininity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perfume associated with women, especially perfume that colors clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with perfumes characterized as masculine because they leave no color or mark.

cautions: The Quranic use in 4:117 and the related designation of deities has both a grammatical-feminine interpretation and a semantic interpretation based on inanimacy and lack of agency.
